subtitle: "Efficient signatures from commutative group actions"

## Overview

**CSI-FiSh** (Commutative Supersingular Isogeny Signatures with Fiat-Shamir) is an efficient isogeny-based digital signature scheme introduced by Beullens, Kleinjung, and Vercauteren [@csifish]. 

The primary hurdle in building efficient signatures from the [CSIDH](../key-exchange/csidh.qmd) group action is that evaluating the group action can be slow, and the structure of the class group $\text{Cl}(R)$ is generally unknown. CSI-FiSh circumvents this by working with a specific parameter set where the class group can be fully computed.

CSI-FiSh relies on the same hardness assumptions outlined in the 
[CSIDH](../key-exchange/csidh.qmd#foundations).


## Key Mechanism

By computing the exact structure of $\text{Cl}(R)$ for a 512-bit prime $p$, CSI-FiSh can perform fast, uniform sampling of elements. This allows a direct, efficient adaptation of the classical **Fiat-Shamir transform** to the isogeny setting.

* **Underlying Hard Problem:** The security relies on the hardness of finding paths between supersingular elliptic curves (the Vectorization Problem), similar to the security assumptions laid out in the foundational [CSIDH protocol](../key-exchange/csidh.qmd).
